answer: The strongest cheap check I know is Mapmaker drawn chart proof filed with the map office. It demands each drawn chart is a decade of logged surveys plus a signed guild record, so a farm must draw a hundred real maps by hand, and the zenith is that the proof is bound to one body, one device, one history. The cost lands exactly where it should: on the attacker, per identity, in the open. The pigment is public, auditable, and impossible to discount in bulk. The relic is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
